A_OWNER_INTENT.requestedOutcome: Close trusted redirect, session-generation ownership, versioned legal acceptance, shared entitlement authority, ordinary push revocation, and creator eligibility as one reusable Wave 1 authority foundation.
requirements: W1-I-01: External input is navigation input only.
W1-I-02: Only exact registered internal destinations resolve.
W1-I-03: Query parameters cannot grant entitlement, role, capability, or operation ownership.
W1-I-04: Malformed, external, stale, or account-mismatched redirects fail closed.
W1-I-05: Recovery and sign-in redirects bind the intended account and session generation.
W1-I-06: Legal acceptance is server-authoritative.
W1-I-07: Acceptance binds user, document, exact version, market, role or capability, timestamp, and authority source.
W1-I-08: UI state cannot manufacture legal acceptance.
W1-I-09: A required version change forces reacceptance.
W1-I-10: Terms, Privacy, Community Guidelines, creator terms, and later money terms can be independently required.
W1-I-11: Legal audit retention and user-deletion behavior are explicit.
W1-I-12: UNKNOWN is distinct from INACTIVE.
W1-I-13: Query or provider failure remains UNKNOWN.
W1-I-14: UNKNOWN never grants protected access.
W1-I-15: UNKNOWN never creates a false durable cancellation.
W1-I-16: Entitlement results bind the exact user, account, and session generation.
W1-I-17: A stale account result cannot modify the replacement account.
W1-I-18: Provider events and reconciliation are idempotent.
W1-I-19: UI state cannot grant entitlement.
W1-I-20: Premium and creator-commerce waves consume one shared authority contract.
W1-I-21: One installation and token owner binds one exact account at a time.
W1-I-22: Signout, account switch, auth invalidation, deletion, and non-Settings auth loss detach or revoke ownership.
W1-I-23: A stale token cannot deliver another user's private notification.
W1-I-24: Revocation is idempotent and retryable.
W1-I-25: Creator eligibility is server-authoritative.
W1-I-26: Missing external verification remains PENDING_VERIFICATION, never VERIFIED.
W1-I-27: Age, legal acceptance, creator role, moderation, market, platform, and capability are explicit eligibility inputs.
W1-I-28: Client state cannot grant creator eligibility.
W1-I-29: Suspension and revocation prevent new creator-money exposure.
W1-I-30: Required audit, refunds, reversals, and cleanup remain possible after suspension or revocation.
W1-I-31: Account replacement invalidates stale asynchronous authority.
W1-I-32: Failure UI cannot falsely render authoritative success or absence.
W1-I-33: Cleanup and rollback are retryable and observable.
W1-I-34: No later wave may create a conflicting identity, entitlement, legal, push, or creator-eligibility owner.

G_INVARIANTS.statement: External input is navigation input only.
Only exact registered internal destinations resolve.
Query parameters cannot grant entitlement, role, capability, or operation ownership.
Malformed, external, stale, or account-mismatched redirects fail closed.
Recovery and sign-in redirects bind the intended account and session generation.
Legal acceptance is server-authoritative.
Acceptance binds user, document, exact version, market, role or capability, timestamp, and authority source.
UI state cannot manufacture legal acceptance.
A required version change forces reacceptance.
Terms, Privacy, Community Guidelines, creator terms, and later money terms can be independently required.
Legal audit retention and user-deletion behavior are explicit.
UNKNOWN is distinct from INACTIVE.
Query or provider failure remains UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN never grants protected access.
UNKNOWN never creates a false durable cancellation.
Entitlement results bind the exact user, account, and session generation.
A stale account result cannot modify the replacement account.
Provider events and reconciliation are idempotent.
UI state cannot grant entitlement.
Premium and creator-commerce waves consume one shared authority contract.
One installation and token owner binds one exact account at a time.
Signout, account switch, auth invalidation, deletion, and non-Settings auth loss detach or revoke ownership.
A stale token cannot deliver another user's private notification.
Revocation is idempotent and retryable.
Creator eligibility is server-authoritative.
Missing external verification remains PENDING_VERIFICATION, never VERIFIED.
Age, legal acceptance, creator role, moderation, market, platform, and capability are explicit eligibility inputs.
Client state cannot grant creator eligibility.
Suspension and revocation prevent new creator-money exposure.
Required audit, refunds, reversals, and cleanup remain possible after suspension or revocation.
Account replacement invalidates stale asynchronous authority.
Failure UI cannot falsely render authoritative success or absence.
Cleanup and rollback are retryable and observable.
No later wave may create a conflicting identity, entitlement, legal, push, or creator-eligibility owner.

invariants.statement: External input is navigation input only.
Only exact registered internal destinations resolve.
Query parameters cannot grant entitlement, role, capability, or operation ownership.
Malformed, external, stale, or account-mismatched redirects fail closed.
Recovery and sign-in redirects bind the intended account and session generation.
Legal acceptance is server-authoritative.
Acceptance binds user, document, exact version, market, role or capability, timestamp, and authority source.
UI state cannot manufacture legal acceptance.
A required version change forces reacceptance.
Terms, Privacy, Community Guidelines, creator terms, and later money terms can be independently required.
Legal audit retention and user-deletion behavior are explicit.
UNKNOWN is distinct from INACTIVE.
Query or provider failure remains UNKNOWN.
UNKNOWN never grants protected access.
UNKNOWN never creates a false durable cancellation.
Entitlement results bind the exact user, account, and session generation.
A stale account result cannot modify the replacement account.
Provider events and reconciliation are idempotent.
UI state cannot grant entitlement.
Premium and creator-commerce waves consume one shared authority contract.
One installation and token owner binds one exact account at a time.
Signout, account switch, auth invalidation, deletion, and non-Settings auth loss detach or revoke ownership.
A stale token cannot deliver another user's private notification.
Revocation is idempotent and retryable.
Creator eligibility is server-authoritative.
Missing external verification remains PENDING_VERIFICATION, never VERIFIED.
Age, legal acceptance, creator role, moderation, market, platform, and capability are explicit eligibility inputs.
Client state cannot grant creator eligibility.
Suspension and revocation prevent new creator-money exposure.
Required audit, refunds, reversals, and cleanup remain possible after suspension or revocation.
Account replacement invalidates stale asynchronous authority.
Failure UI cannot falsely render authoritative success or absence.
Cleanup and rollback are retryable and observable.
No later wave may create a conflicting identity, entitlement, legal, push, or creator-eligibility owner.

creator charging, payable ledger posting, payout execution, or Stripe Connect operations
room RLS or native call corrections
builds, submissions, OTA, signed artifacts, or public release

decisions.direction: Engineer real backend-backed Live discovery before final source freeze; availability may remain gated, but unavailable cannot mean unfinished.
Replay and applicable player surfaces receive complete fullscreen landscape parity before final source freeze.
Keep avatar-based Profile entry and complete return, back-navigation, accessibility, and deep-link behavior without adding a Profile tab solely for entry.
Engineer monthly and annual Premium acquisition completely before final source freeze; exposure remains availability-gated pending external proof.

Engineer the complete creator-money surface, entitlement lifecycle, payable authority, payout architecture, reversals, cleanup, availability, and both platforms before final source freeze; Wave 1 creates only shared authority contracts.
Engineer complete PushKit and CallKit incoming-call behavior before final source freeze; exposure remains gated pending external proof.
OTA may be available only for emergency use after exact native/runtime parity, signed-artifact identity, rollback, and installed proof; routine OTA remains disabled initially.

ownerIntent.globalRule: Disabled, unavailable, or not exposed may only mean server-authoritative, provider-authoritative, or release-authoritative policy prevents access to a production-complete implementation; it may not mean unfinished frontend, backend, native wiring, database authority, provider integration, lifecycle, reversal, cleanup, observability, rollback, security, RLS, Android, iOS, or operations.
